ns2:section.sectionText: SP25 ENGL 396 - English Honors Seminar - Nineteenth-Century American Literature and Capitalism - John Barnard - This honors seminar will focus on literary and journalistic engagements with the rise of industrial and finance capitalism in the late-nineteenth and early-twentieth centuries. We will attend specifically to the relation between capitalist social relations and literary form, especially the genres of realism and naturalism, as well as examples of speculative fiction. While the course will be historical, we will also consider the relevance of this period and these works for us today, as we are now in what is often called a “Second Gilded Age,” in which economic inequality and ecological crises have once again brought the sustainability of capitalism as a system into question. Authors might include: Rebecca Harding Davis, Elizabeth Stuart Phelps, Edward Bellamy, T. Thomas Fortune, William Dean Howells, Mark Twain, Ida B. Wells, Upton Sinclair, and Edith Wharton.
